title: Enhanced electromagnetic wave absorption property of binary ZnO/NiCo2O4 composites

nodes.label: Microwave absorbers need strong loss together with impedance matching; single-component oxides give one or the other
A binary ZnO/NiCo2O4 hybrid should add heterointerfaces whose interfacial polarisation raises dielectric loss and so the absorption
ZnO as the host semiconductor particle
Grow NiCo2O4 on and around the ZnO particles from Ni2+ and Co2+ in the same bath
NH3.H2O addition 0.5, 0.7 and 1.0 mL, giving ZnO/NiCo2O4-5, -7 and -10
Hydrothermal reaction at 200 C for 18 h: OH- precipitates Zn(OH)2 and NiCo2(OH)6 nuclei form on it
Calcination at 300 C for 2 h in air converts both hydroxides to ZnO and NiCo2O4 at once
Powder mixed 1:1 by mass with paraffin into a coaxial toroid, complex permittivity and permeability measured 2.0-18.0 GHz
Two phases only: hexagonal ZnO (PDF 99-0111) and spinel NiCo2O4 (PDF 20-0781), no impurity phase in any sample
NiCo2O4 nano-dots sit in direct lattice contact with the ZnO, giving a dense array of ZnO/NiCo2O4 heterointerfaces inside each aggregate
Alkalinity sets the morphology: irregular nanoparticle aggregates at 0.5 and 0.7 mL, porous plate-like sheets decorated with nanoparticles at 1.0 mL
All three powders are mesoporous (type IV isotherms, pores mainly 0-40 nm); BET area 86.85, 22.57 and 80.13 m2/g for -5, -7 and -10
Complex permittivity rises with NH3.H2O content: maximum real part 5.78, 6.85, 6.96 and imaginary part about 0.33, 0.48, 0.67 at 18 GHz
The powders are essentially non-magnetic (Ms 0.0007 emu/g, Hc 60 Oe), so magnetic loss is argued to play little part
Dielectric loss tangent and attenuation constant both rise with NH3.H2O content and with frequency, reaching alpha about 84, 73 and 55 at 18 GHz for -10, -7 and -5
Charge redistributes across the many ZnO/NiCo2O4 boundaries under the alternating field, so several Debye relaxations dissipate the wave
Eddy-current loss is excluded as the magnetic-loss mechanism because C0 is not constant with frequency
Impedance matching is reached only by -7 and -10, above about 13 GHz and above 3.4 mm thickness; -5 never gets the matching parameter below 0.4
ZnO/NiCo2O4-7 absorbs best: minimum reflection loss -33.49 dB at 18.0 GHz and 4.99 mm, against -27.46 dB for -10 and only -6.52 dB for -5

attrs.condition: 2-18 GHz, 1.0-5.0 mm layer, 50 wt% in paraffin

nodes.label: A binary ZnO/NiCo2O4 hybrid tuned by alkalinity gives a purely dielectric Ku-band absorber reaching -33.49 dB
The composite is useful only in the Ku band and needs a layer thicker than about 3 mm; NH3.H2O near 0.7 mL gives the best compromise
The reflection loss passes -10 dB only above about 17 GHz, i.e. in roughly 1 GHz at the very edge of the measured band
Every reflection in the three patterns carries a star (ZnO) or a diamond (NiCo2O4) marker; no unmarked peak is left

C0 = mu'' (mu')^-2 f^-1: a frequency-independent C0 means eddy-current loss
Debye theory makes the plot of imaginary against real permittivity a semicircle, one per relaxation process
Transmission-line theory gives the reflection loss from the complex parameters and thickness; matching is judged by |delta| < 0.4 and dissipation by the attenuation constant
ZnO is a non-magnetic semiconductor and NiCo2O4 is non-magnetic at room temperature

notes: Everything downstream of the permittivity/permeability measurement is computed from it, so the C0, Cole-Cole, delta, alpha and reflection-loss readouts hang on derives edges from the raw parameter node r7. The magnetic branch is a control branch that ends in a non-magnetic PRP and an eddy-current MEC/identification. Lost: the reaction equations, the VSM figure (F4, not opened) and the BET/BJH figure (F3, not opened, so c12 rests on a text-only OBS). Image findings that bear on the argument: the dielectric loss tangent and the attenuation constant are highest for ZnO/NiCo2O4-10, not for the best absorber -7 (r8, r14), so the record's summary claim that -7 has the highest loss tangent and alpha is wrong; the magnetic loss tangent exceeds the dielectric one over almost the whole band, against the claim that magnetic loss is negligible (r10); the reflection loss passes -10 dB only above about 17 GHz (r16, c22); the -7 sample has the smallest BET area of the three, which the paper never reconciles with its best absorption; the Cole-Cole loci show one arc plus a near-vertical rise rather than three semicircles (r12); in the EDS maps only Ni is discontinuous, Co is nearly as uniform as Zn (r5); the SEM panels do not distinguish the -5 and -7 morphologies (r2). Packet problems: the running text of the paper cites Fig. 8(b), 8(d) and 8(f) for the -7, -10 and -5 minima, one row off from the caption and from the colour bars; the F2b cue line reads 'scale bar 0.26 nm', which is the marked d-spacing, not the 10 nm bar; the F3a crop is labelled 'letter l (OCR DISAGREES with detector a)'.

changes: r13: OBS/response/regime_map -> OBS/response/trend with attrs.dimension = 2D. v04's written sibling rule is 'a single response's contours over two variables is trend (dimension=2D); boundaries between qualitatively different states is regime_map'. The F7 panels are continuous colour contours of one quantity (the matching parameter) over frequency and thickness; the matched/unmatched split comes from the externally imposed |delta| < 0.4 criterion, not from a state boundary in the material. The mm_op read_characteristic_point is unchanged - r04 ruling #6 already puts 'locating a sample relative to a boundary' there - and c18 reads the same thing either way.

panel_checks.note: the EDS strip shows Co nearly as even as Zn and only Ni visibly clustered, so the node is right that the text's 'both Ni and Co discontinuous' is not what the maps show

the -10 trace (blue) is highest at every frequency and reaches about 0.10 at 18 GHz while -7 (red) reaches about 0.07, with -5 (black) touching or crossing it around 10-13 GHz; the record's claim that the best absorber has the highest loss tangent does not survive this panel

panel (c) is the -7 map and its colour bar bottoms at -33.50 dB, in the top-right corner near 18 GHz and 5 mm. This also settles the packet/text conflict in the node's favour: the paper's running text cites 8(d) for this minimum, i.e. its panel letters are one row off, and the graph follows the image. F7a was opened as a spot check and its colour bar reads 0.55, as r13 states.

review.audit_summary: 3 audits (c22 the -10 dB band being about 1 GHz wide at the edge of the measurement, r8 and r10 contradicting the paper's loss-mechanism reading). All three genuinely change support for c19 and c14, and each is phrased as a panel reading with the panel named. The r10 audit is the strongest and is correctly built from two panels on a shared abscissa via compare_coplotted_quantities.
